PDS Biotechnology announced September 22 that results from its VERSATILE-002 Phase 2 trial are now published in JAMA Oncology, putting the data into the peer-reviewed record rather than the conference-abstract circuit where clinical claims often circulate without full scrutiny. The trial tested PDS0101, an HPV16-targeted immunotherapy, combined with pembrolizumab in patients with HPV16-positive recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. The 39.3-month median overall survival figure comes from the modified intention-to-treat population with a PD-L1 Combined Positive Score of at least 1, the patients most likely to respond to checkpoint inhibition. That population is also the commercial sweet spot, since PD-L1 CPS guides pembrolizumab dosing decisions in standard practice, and a survival signal this durable in a combination regimen will draw direct comparisons to pembrolizumab monotherapy benchmarks already in the literature. Publication in a peer-reviewed journal matters beyond prestige. Payers, guideline committees, and potential partners weigh journal-level evidence differently than data presented at a conference or posted on ClinicalTrials.gov. The JAMA Oncology appearance gives VERSATILE-002 the citation permanence that supports a biologics license application narrative and gives investigators a citable reference when designing follow-on studies or combination arms. PDS Biotechnology is a small company, and having this dataset anchored in a high-impact journal strengthens the hand of anyone evaluating a licensing or co-development conversation. The trial was Phase 2, so the survival figure carries the usual caveats about sample size and the absence of a randomized comparator arm. The next concrete marker is whether PDS Biotechnology uses the JAMA Oncology publication as the scientific foundation to advance toward a registrational study, and whether a larger partner moves first to claim the HPV16-targeted combination space in head and neck cancer. content: PDS Biotech's HPV16 cancer immunotherapy posts 39.3-month survival in JAMA Oncology ● 3 days ago What happened? On 2026-09-22, PDS Biotechnology announced the publication of final survival data from its Phase ️2 VERSATILE-002 trial in JAMA Oncology. The study evaluated PDS0101, an experimental immunotherapy designed to activate T cells against tumours caused by the HPV16 virus, combined with pembrolizumab(Keytruda(, in people with recurrent or metastatic head-and-neck cancer. In patients without prior checkpoint-inhibitor therapy whose tumours expressed the PD-L1 protein(CPS≥1(, median overall survival was 39.3 months——far longer than the roughly ️17.9-month benchmark cited for standard pembrolizumab-based care, though comparisons across different trials need caution. Why it matters: Head-and-neck cancer that returns or spreads is hard to treat,ands survival beyond three years in this setting is unusually long. These results were published in the ️2026-09-17 issue of JAMA Oncology,and are among the strongest reported for HPV16-positive patients. PDS0101 works by training the immune system to attack cancer cells displaying viral proteins, offering a potentially durable response for patients whose tumours are driven by HPV16, which accounts for a sizeable share of head-and-neck cancers. The company says the data support its goal of bringing PDS0101 to patients with limited options,and it is engaging with regulators on next steps toward approval. Kovina Therapeutics Awarded $2.3 Million NCI Grant to Advance First-in-Class HPV Cancer Therapy Directly Targeting E6 Business Wire Thu, September 24, 2026 at 6:00 AM MDT 3 min read Direct-to-Phase II SBIR award supports IND-enabling development of Kovina's lead oral small molecule program INDIANAPOLIS, September 24, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Kovina Therapeutics Inc., a biotechnology company developing first-in-class small molecule therapeutics targeting the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) E6 oncoprotein, today announced a $2.3 million Direct-to-Phase II Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) award from the National Cancer Institute (NCI). The two-year award will support IND-enabling development of Kovina's lead oral small molecule program for HPV-driven cancers. The award follows Kovina's recent publication in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS) validating direct pharmacologic targeting of HPV E6. The research demonstrated restoration of p53 tumor suppressor activity, selective killing of HPV-positive cancer cells and tumor growth inhibition in HPV-positive preclinical models. "This award comes at an important point for Kovina as we move from compelling preclinical science into formal development," said Kristin Sherman, Chief Executive Officer of Kovina Therapeutics. "Together with our recent PNAS publication, the NCI support gives us significant momentum as we advance our lead program through IND-enabling development and toward the clinic." HPV E6 is a viral oncoprotein that degrades the tumor suppressor p53 and is required for the survival of HPV-positive cancer cells. Kovina's small molecules are designed to inhibit E6 and restore p53 function, offering a targeted approach to the underlying mechanism of these cancers. The NCI award will support key development activities, including CMC, IND-enabling pharmacology and toxicology, and other studies required to support an Investigational New Drug application. "HPV E6 has long been recognized as a compelling cancer target but directly inhibiting it with a small molecule has been challenging," said Elliot Androphy, M.D., Founder and Chief Scientific Officer of Kovina Therapeutics. "Our work demonstrates that E6 can be specifically targeted, restoring p53 and selectively killing HPV-positive cancer cells. This gives us a strong foundation for translating the biology into a new therapeutic approach." Despite preventive vaccines, HPV causes an estimated 39,300 cancers each year in the United States, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, including cervical and head and neck cancers. By directly targeting HPV E6, Kovina's approach has the potential to treat a spectrum of HPV-associated disease, from premalignant disease to invasive cancers. The company is advancing its lead oral program toward clinical development. To learn more, visit www.kovina.com. content: 要闻 时政 紫牛头条 全景苏超 问政江苏 紫牛号 天下事 社会 文娱 体育 扬子时评 教育 健康 科技 文旅 财汇 房产 汽车 聚场 江苏 南京 苏州 无锡 B座西窗 微史记 少年志 首页 > 新闻中心 > 健康 开学季做好健康计划 江苏为适龄人群提供多元化的HPV疫苗接种选择 来源: 紫牛新闻 2026-09-23 15:57:00 秋季新学期已经拉开帷幕,在做好季节性传染病防控的同时,适龄女孩HPV疫苗接种同样值得家长列入新学期健康计划。宫颈癌是目前世界上唯一病因明确的恶性肿瘤,而接种HPV疫苗,正是从源头阻断HPV感染最经济、最有效的手段。江苏省正通过“国家免疫规划免费接种+地方惠民活动减免”双轨并行模式,为适龄人群提供多元化的HPV疫苗接种选择。 小年龄段接种免疫效果更好 早预防早保护 宫颈癌是严重威胁女性健康的公共卫生问题。几乎所有的宫颈癌(99%以上)都与高危型HPV持续感染密切相关。在中国,常见的感染型别为HPV52、16、58。近年来,我国宫颈癌发病率呈上升趋势,宫颈癌发病年龄呈现年轻化趋势,部分病例甚至出现在20多岁未育女性中。 同时,宫颈癌是一种可以预防的癌症,2023年中国《子宫颈癌综合防控指南(第2版)》提出了三级预防策略,其中,一级预防的主要措施包括开展健康教育和接种预防性HPV疫苗;二级预防强调早筛早诊;三级预防则是对已确诊的宫颈癌患者进行规范治疗。 世界卫生组织明确推荐:9-14岁未发生性行为的女孩是首要接种人群。从感染风险看,HPV主要通过性行为传播,首次性行为前接种可获得更好的保护效果;从免疫效果看,9-14岁女孩接种后产生的抗体水平是15岁以上人群的2倍以上,保护效果可持续至少10年。 自2023年起,江苏省把“为适龄女生免费接种HPV疫苗”纳入省政府民生实事项目,按照“知情、同意、自愿”的原则,为全省初一女生免费接种国产双价HPV疫苗。此后,HPV疫苗也被纳入国家免疫规划。我国将13周岁女孩确定为HPV疫苗免费接种人群,是综合考虑保护效果、成本效益和可操作性而确定的最优方案。 目前,除免疫规划疫苗为适龄女孩免费提供外,还有多种非免疫规划HPV疫苗供受种者自愿、自费接种。如适龄女孩已按照相应价次疫苗的免疫程序完成全程接种,同样视为完成国家HPV疫苗免疫规划接种。 部分年龄段减免将截止 抓紧9月30日窗口接种 从年龄来看,中国女性HPV感染率按年龄呈“双峰”分布:第一个高峰在17-24岁,这与年轻女性处于性活跃初期有关;第二个高峰在40-44岁。大年龄段女性的免疫功能可能会随年龄增加而下降,对新发和既往感染的清除能力也会随之下降,从而可能更容易发生持续感染,所以接种HPV疫苗对成年女性也十分有必要。 在全球范围内,90%的男性在其一生中至少感染一次HPV,男性生殖器HPV的感染率实际上高于女性,男性感染HPV后可能导致肛门癌、阴茎癌、口咽癌和尖锐湿疣。HPV疫苗不仅可以预防女性宫颈癌,还可以预防男性感染HPV引起的肛门癌和生殖器疣等。 由中华医学会妇科肿瘤学分会等七个学会共同制定发布的《预防性人乳头瘤病毒疫苗中国临床应用指南(2025版)》,优先推荐9-26岁女性接种HPV疫苗,其中9-14岁女孩是重点人群;同时推荐27-45岁女性和9-26岁男性接种。 为落实《“健康中国2030”规划纲要》和《江苏省加速消除宫颈癌行动计划实施方案(2023—2030年)》等文件要求,江苏省多地推出了适龄人群HPV疫苗接种惠民活动,并且将男性也纳入惠民范围,满足了更多样化的健康防护需求。 值得关注的是,根据江苏多地发布的信息,从2026年10月1日起,进口九价HPV疫苗惠民减免接种活动将调整,惠民人群范围也有所调整。其中,9-14岁女性、18-26岁女性及18-26岁男性接种进口九价HPV疫苗,可减免一针费用。其中,9-14岁女生只需接种2剂次,第二剂次免费。惠民活动首针接种结束时间延长至2027年12月31日。自2026年10月1日起,15-17周岁女性、35-45周岁女性、16-17周岁男性不再纳入进口九价HPV疫苗惠民范围。上述人群如要享受惠民减免,须在2026年9月30日前完成首针接种,且在2027年3月31日前完成全程接种。因各区县惠民活动起止时间可能不一致,具体以当地出台接种活动细则为准。 预约就近接种。其他居民同样可通过APP预约,或咨询当地接种门诊。同时,为提高公众科学认知,江苏省聘请省人民医院妇科主任程文俊和省广电总台主持人胡馨尹担任“预防接种公益宣传大使”,为HPV疫苗接种等预防接种工作提供权威专业科普指导。
